bianhe.name: 汴河
bianhe.long: 過了城鄉交界，汴河流進畫面。這條運河自洛口引黃河水，東流入淮，東南的糧米貨物都由它運進京城。宋太宗說過，京城「養兵數十萬，居人百萬家」，全仰這一渠水。岸邊泊著吃水很深的糧船，腳夫扛著糧袋上岸，船主坐在貨包上歇息；沿河一條街多是飯館茶肆，臨河的雅座開窗對著水面。高處一座望火樓卻空無一人，余輝讀作繁華底下的隱憂。
bianhe.quote: 運東南之糧，凡東南方物，自此入京城，公私仰給焉。
bianhe.cite: 《東京夢華錄》・故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉
bianhe.long_en: Past the line where town meets country, the Bian Canal flows into the picture. It draws Yellow River water at Luokou and runs east to the Huai, and the grain and goods of the south-east come into the capital along it. Emperor Taizong of Song said the capital, which “keeps hundreds of thousands of soldiers and a million households,” depended wholly on this one channel. Deep-laden grain boats are moored along the bank, porters carry sacks ashore, and a boat-owner rests on his bundles; the street along the water is mostly eating houses and teahouses, their riverside seats opening windows onto the water. A fire-watch tower on high ground stands empty, which Yu Hui reads as a worry hidden beneath the prosperity.
bianhe.quote_en: Bringing in the grain of the south-east: all the goods of the south-east enter the capital this way, and public and private households alike depend on it.
bianhe.cite_en: Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights

juanwei.name: 卷尾
juanwei.long: 長卷到此收束。余輝說，畫家在結尾留下「三問」：趙太丞家門前問病，「解」字招牌下問命，官宦人家門口問道。街上一位戴寬簷帽的官人騎馬出行；提著食盒的外鄉人順著守門人的手指望去，兩旁街樹相合，畫卷卻戛然而止。徐邦達疑心「後面是割去了不少的」，鄭振鐸以為原畫應一直畫到金明池。畫後接著的，是金、元、明歷代文人的題跋。
juanwei.quote: 翰林張擇端，字正道，東武人也。幼讀書，遊學於京師。
juanwei.cite: 余輝〈最後三問〉・故宮名畫記・徐邦達・鄭振鐸
juanwei.long_en: Here the long scroll draws to a close. Yu Hui says the painter leaves “three questions” at the end: asking about illness before Imperial Physician Zhao's door, asking about fate under the sign of the character “Jie,” and asking the way at the door of an official family. An official in a wide-brimmed hat rides out along the street; a stranger carrying a food box follows the gatekeeper's pointing finger, the street trees on both sides close together, and the painting simply stops. Xu Bangda suspects that “a good deal was cut off after this,” and Zheng Zhenduo thought the original ran all the way to the Jinming Pond. After the painting come the colophons of scholars of the Jin, Yuan and Ming dynasties.
juanwei.quote_en: The Hanlin academician Zhang Zeduan, courtesy name Zhengdao, was a man of Dongwu. As a boy he read books and went to study in the capital.
juanwei.cite_en: Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Xu Bangda · Zheng Zhenduo

jiaoye.name: 郊野
jiaoye.long: 畫卷由右向左展開，開卷是汴京東南的遠郊：河渠縱橫，老樹還沒抽芽，薄霧輕籠，正是早春。兩個腳夫趕著馱炭的驢隊走向小橋，農家的穀場靜悄悄的；隋堤上一排老柳，掃墓的人家抬著插滿楊柳的轎子回城。畫的是不是清明，學者有過爭論：孔憲易據炭驢、扇子和「新酒」旗，以為是秋景；金人張著的跋文落款「清明後一日」，余輝以為這已婉轉點明了時節。這裏從清明之說。
jiaoye.quote: 凡新墳皆用此日拜掃。都城人出郊。
jiaoye.cite: 故宮名畫記・孔憲易・余輝〈跋文考釋〉
jiaoye.long_en: The scroll unrolls from right to left, and it opens in the far outskirts south-east of Bianjing: rivers and canals criss-cross, the old trees have not yet leafed, a thin mist hangs over everything, and it is early spring. Two porters drive a train of charcoal-laden donkeys toward a small bridge, and a farmer's threshing floor lies quiet. Along the Sui Embankment stands a row of old willows, and a family returning from sweeping graves carries a sedan chair stuck full of willow twigs back to town. Scholars have argued whether the painting shows Qingming at all: Kong Xianyi, citing the charcoal donkeys, the fans and the “new wine” flag, took it for autumn; the colophon by the Jin writer Zhang Zhu is signed “the day after Qingming,” which Yu Hui takes as a quiet statement of the season. Here we follow the Qingming reading.
jiaoye.quote_en: All new graves are visited on this day. The people of the capital go out to the suburbs.
jiaoye.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Kong Xianyi · Yu Hui, Notes on the Colophons

chengmen.name: 城門
chengmen.long: 過了護城河上的平橋，便是全卷最高大的建築：城樓。這是哪一座城門，說法不一：故宮從東角子門之說；徐邦達、張安治據金人張公藥的跋詩「水門東去接隋渠」讀作東水門；余輝則說門額上只寫一個「門」字，畫的是「實情而非實景」。這裏用故宮之說。余輝又指出，這座城門沒有甕城，也不見垛口；一隊駱駝正從門洞走出城去，牽頭的像是胡人，進門頭一家便是稅務。
chengmen.quote: 城門前後、城樓上下竟然沒有一兵一卒把守。
chengmen.quoteSrc: 余輝〈清明上河圖十大看點〉
chengmen.cite: 故宮・徐邦達・張安治・余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉
chengmen.long_en: Across the flat bridge over the moat stands the tallest building in the whole scroll: the gate tower. Which gate it is, no one agrees: the Palace Museum follows the Dongjiaozi Gate reading; Xu Bangda and Zhang Anzhi, citing the line “The water gate eastward meets the Sui canal” in the colophon poem by the Jin writer Zhang Gongyao, read it as the East Water Gate; Yu Hui says the plaque bears only the single character “Gate,” and that the painter shows “the true situation, not the real view.” Here we use the Palace Museum's reading. Yu Hui also points out that this gate has no barbican and no crenellations; a string of camels is walking out of the gateway and out of the city, led by what looks like a man from the Western lands, and the first shop inside the gate is the Tax Office.
chengmen.quote_en: Before and behind the gate, above and below the gate tower, there is not a single soldier standing guard.
chengmen.cite_en: Palace Museum · Xu Bangda · Zhang Anzhi · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions

shizijie.name: 十字街
shizijie.sub_en: The Busy Market Inside the City
shizijie.long: 進了城門，便是畫中最熱鬧的市街。余輝說這一段從城門內經十字路口，一直到水井為止，畫家「以孫記正店為中心」。正店門前彩樓高搭，兩頂媒婆的轎子正要在門口落下；肉鋪前圍了一圈人聽說書；十字路口，騾子拉的大車急轉過街角。香藥鋪、客店、醫鋪、綢緞鋪一家挨著一家，士子、僧人、挑夫、閒人擠在同一條街上。余輝為這一段取的題目是「鬧市繁華顯不平」。
shizijie.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》
shizijie.long_en: Inside the gate lies the liveliest market street in the painting. Yu Hui says this stretch, from just inside the gate across the crossroads to the well, is where the painter “centres on the Sun establishment's main tavern.” In front of the tavern a festive tower is raised high, and two go-between ladies' sedans are about to set down at its door; in front of the butcher's a circle of people listens to a storyteller; at the crossroads a mule-drawn cart swings sharply round the corner. Incense shops, inns, doctors' shops and silk shops stand one after another, and scholars, monks, porters and idlers all crowd the same street. Yu Hui's title for this stretch is “The Busy Market Shows Inequality Amid Its Splendour.”
shizijie.quote_en: After long years of peace, the people were many and the goods plentiful.
shizijie.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital

chengmenkouwai.name: 城門口外
chengmenkouwai.long: 離了河岸，大路往西直通城門。余輝把這一段叫作「城門口外真悠閒」：車鋪裏匠人在修車輪，兩輛棕蓋大車一停一走，小鋪裏有人閒坐吃茶，算命先生的攤子支在官衙旁邊；遞鋪門前的兵卒或坐或臥，院裏一匹白馬也躺著歇息。再往西，寺院山門緊閉，牛拉的大蓋車疾行而來，正和一位騎馬的人在街角相逢，悠閒裏也夾著幾分緊張。
chengmenkouwai.quote: 從城外守門入城貨賣，至天明不絕。
chengmenkouwai.quoteSrc: 《東京夢華錄》卷三〈天曉諸人入市〉
chengmenkouwai.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記
chengmenkouwai.long_en: Leaving the riverbank, the main road runs west straight to the city gate. Yu Hui calls this stretch “Truly Leisurely Outside the Gate”: in a cart shop a craftsman mends a wheel, two palm-roofed carts, one halted and one moving, pass each other, in a small shop someone sits drinking tea, and a fortune-teller's stall is set up beside the government office. Soldiers at the dispatch post sit or lie at the door, and in the yard a white horse lies resting too. Further west, a temple's main gate is shut tight, and an ox-drawn covered cart hurries up and meets a rider at the street corner, a little tension mixed into the ease.
chengmenkouwai.quote_en: People come from outside the gate to sell goods in the city, and it goes on without a break until dawn.
chengmenkouwai.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji

hongqiao.name: 虹橋
hongqiao.long: 長卷行到中段，便是全畫最驚險的一幕。一條大船正要穿過虹橋，桅桿還沒放倒，船工有的撐篙抵住橋身，有的大聲呼喊；橋上的人探身拋下繩索，看熱鬧的擠滿了橋欄。橋面上，一頂轎子和一位騎馬的官人迎面相逢，隨從各不相讓。余輝說這是全卷矛盾的高潮；曹星原更把這場搶險讀作全畫的主旨「同舟共濟」。橋頭，十千腳店的彩樓歡門高高搭起。
hongqiao.quote: 畫橋虹臥浚儀渠，兩岸風煙天下無。
hongqiao.quoteSrc: 金元之際 張世積跋
hongqiao.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉・曹星原・韓森
hongqiao.long_en: In the middle of the long scroll comes the most nerve-racking scene in the whole painting. A big boat is about to pass under the Rainbow Bridge, its mast not yet lowered; some boatmen brace poles against the bridge, others shout at the top of their voices, and people on the bridge lean over to throw down ropes while onlookers crowd the railings. On the deck of the bridge, a sedan chair and an official on horseback meet head-on, and the retinues give no ground. Yu Hui says this is the climax of the conflicts in the whole scroll; Cao Xingyuan reads this rescue as the painting's central theme, “all in the same boat.” At the bridgehead, the festive welcome gate of the Shiqian Tavern is raised high.
hongqiao.quote_en: The painted bridge lies like a rainbow over the Junyi canal; the mist and wind on both banks have no equal under heaven.
hongqiao.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · Cao Xingyuan · Hansen

S2.bld.yanhe_yazuo_hall_25690.long: 從河邊停泊的船隻看，這裏是個大碼頭。臨河一座長廳架在岸上，一排大窗全敞著，窗裏擺著長桌和交腳的坐具，西頭窗下坐著一位客人，身旁還有個小些的人影。故宮名畫記說，客人在這裏一邊飲酒，一邊看河上風景；乘船來的客人，興許也會拉著船主上岸喝兩杯。長廳東頭同一道屋頂下，是一座門扇緊閉的倉房。
S2.bld.yanhe_yazuo_hall_25690.cite: 故宮名畫記・畫中所見
S2.bld.yanhe_yazuo_hall_25690.long_en: Judging by the boats moored along the bank, this is a big wharf. A long hall stands on the shore beside the water with a row of wide windows thrown open; inside are long tables and folding stools, and a guest sits at the west window with a smaller figure beside him. The Palace Museum's notes say the guest is drinking while he watches the river, and that travellers arriving by boat might also pull the boatman ashore for a cup or two. At the east end of the hall, under the same roof, is a storehouse with its doors shut tight.
S2.bld.yanhe_yazuo_hall_25690.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · What the painting shows

S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.long: 丁字路口有一家專賣紙紮冥器的鋪子，門前立著高高的招牌，學者讀作「王家紙馬」；鋪前一座木架，紙錢紙馬一直疊到屋簷。故宮名畫記說，宋人不像唐人那樣厚葬，多用紙做的錢和冥器代替實物，這風俗一直流傳到今天。招牌前，一位戴著高帽兜的人騎驢停下，正朝鋪子張望。
S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.quote: 紙馬鋪皆於當街用紙袞疊成樓閣之狀。
S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.cite: 故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.long_en: At a T-junction stands a shop that sells nothing but paper offerings for the dead, with a tall sign out front that scholars read as “Wang Family Paper Horses.” In front is a wooden frame with paper money and paper horses piled up to the eaves. The Palace Museum's notes say the Song, unlike the Tang, did not bury the dead with lavish goods but used paper money and paper models in place of the real things, a custom that has lasted to this day. In front of the sign, a rider in a tall hood has stopped his donkey and is looking toward the shop.
S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.quote_en: The paper-horse shops all pile up paper into the shape of towers and pavilions right in the street.
S2.bld.wang_paper_horse_shop_27100.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.long: 磚砌的高臺上一座小亭，一道木梯從西邊攀上臺頂。照《東京夢華錄》，京城的望火樓樓上該有人瞭望，樓下駐著兵士，備著水桶、麻搭、梯子，一見火起便奔報撲救。畫中這座卻空無一人，余輝說臺上原本的高柱被截去大半，改成了供人歇息的涼亭，樓下兩排營房也做了飯鋪。他把這裏讀作「虛設的望火樓」。
S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.quote: 於高處磚砌望火樓，樓上有人卓望。
S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.cite: 《東京夢華錄》・余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.long_en: On a high brick platform stands a small pavilion, with a wooden ladder climbing the platform from the west. According to Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital, a capital fire-watch tower should have a lookout above and soldiers below, with buckets, fire-swabs and ladders ready to run to a fire the moment it is seen. The one in the painting is empty: Yu Hui says the tall posts that once stood on the platform were mostly cut away and turned into a cool pavilion for resting, and the two rows of barracks below became eating shops. He reads it as a “fire tower in name only.”
S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.quote_en: On high ground, a fire-watch tower of brick, with men on top keeping a lookout.
S2.bld.fire_tower_28440.cite_en: Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S2.bld.wanglou_shed_28660.long: 望火樓下一長排草頂棚屋，柱子底下擺滿桌凳，坐著吃喝的客人。余輝以為，這本是望火樓下兵營式的平房，如今改成了飯館。這一帶正是城鄉交界，碼頭對著一條沿河小街，店鋪多賣小吃。故宮名畫記寫街口一景：兩個過路客人卸下驢背上的行李歇腳，店主坐在涼棚下休息，大家的目光都被鄰家小孩的哭聲引了過去。
S2.bld.wanglou_shed_28660.cite: 余輝〈十大看點〉・故宮名畫記・畫中所見
S2.bld.wanglou_shed_28660.long_en: Beneath the fire tower runs a long row of thatched sheds, with tables and benches set out under the posts and customers eating and drinking. Yu Hui believes these were once barracks-style single-storey buildings under the fire tower, now turned into restaurants. This is where town meets country, a wharf facing a small riverside street, and most shops sell snacks. The Palace Museum's notes describe a scene at the corner of the street: two passing travellers have unloaded the baggage from their donkeys to rest, the shopkeeper sits under his awning, and everyone's eyes are drawn by a neighbour's child crying.
S2.bld.wanglou_shed_28660.cite_en: Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · What the painting shows

S7.bld.zhao_taicheng.long: 水井旁又是一家醫鋪，簷下幾塊菱形牌子寫著「趙太丞家」，故宮稱它「國醫趙太丞家」；余輝說趙太丞是侍奉過宮廷的太醫。鋪裏一位穿深色長袍的醫者伸手察看孩子，婦人抱著孩子來求醫。門前立著幾塊高大的招牌，故宮能讀全的一塊寫著「治酒所傷真方集香丸」，柱上一牌還認得出「五勞七傷」。前頭正店、腳店顧客盈門，喝傷了的人想必不少。余輝把這裏讀作結尾「三問」的問病。
S7.bld.zhao_taicheng.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S7.bld.zhao_taicheng.long_en: Beside the well is another medicine shop, with several diamond-shaped boards under the eaves reading “Zhao Taicheng's House”; the Palace Museum calls it the house of “the national physician Zhao Taicheng,” and Yu Hui says Zhao was an imperial doctor who had served the court. Inside, a doctor in a dark robe reaches out to examine a child, and a woman holds the child in to be treated. Out front stand several tall signs; the one the Palace Museum can read in full says “True remedy, Incense Pills, for harm done by wine,” and on a pillar one board still reads “The Five Strains and Seven Injuries.” The taverns ahead are full of customers, so there must have been many who drank too much. Yu Hui reads this as the question about illness among the closing “three questions.”
S7.bld.zhao_taicheng.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S7.bld.gatehouse_1240.long: 趙太丞家隔壁是一座深宅大院，門屋簷下有斗拱，門前有上馬石，看得出是官宦人家。一個外鄉人提著食盒、背著大包袱，在門前停步問路，門口的人伸手往西一指。故宮名畫記寫道：順著他指的方向望去，只見兩旁街樹相合，朦朧一片，畫卷卻在這裏戛然而止。余輝把這一幕讀作結尾「三問」的問道：畫家也在問，這個國家該往哪裏走。
S7.bld.gatehouse_1240.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S7.bld.gatehouse_1240.long_en: Next to Zhao's is a deep courtyard house with brackets under the gatehouse eaves and a mounting stone by the door, plainly the home of an official family. A stranger with a food box in his hand and a large bundle on his back stops at the door to ask the way, and the man at the gate points west. The Palace Museum's notes write: follow where he points and you see the street trees on both sides closing together in a haze, and the painting ends right there. Yu Hui reads this as the question about the way among the closing “three questions”: the painter is also asking where the country should go.
S7.bld.gatehouse_1240.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S1.str.small_bridge_36365.long: 開卷第一景：一座低矮的木板橋，細木柱撐著，橋面鋪著草土，沒有護欄，橋下泊著一隻空船。兩個腳夫趕著馱炭的驢子走向小橋，前頭的腳夫一手扶著領頭驢背上的炭筐。故宮名畫記說，這些炭要運進城裏，供酒店灶下燒火；孔憲易卻拿這隊炭驢作證，說畫的是秋冬而不是清明。
S1.str.small_bridge_36365.cite: 故宮名畫記・孔憲易・畫中所見
S1.str.small_bridge_36365.long_en: The first scene of the scroll: a low wooden plank bridge held up by slender posts, its deck laid with grass and earth and no railing, with an empty boat moored beneath it. Two porters drive charcoal-laden donkeys toward the bridge, and the one in front steadies the charcoal basket on the lead donkey's back with one hand. The Palace Museum's notes say this charcoal is bound for the town to fuel the tavern stoves, while Kong Xianyi cites this very charcoal train as proof that the painting shows autumn or winter, not Qingming.
S1.str.small_bridge_36365.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Kong Xianyi · What the painting shows

S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225.long: 過了小橋，路邊幾間農舍，門前搭著涼棚、擺著椅凳，像是供行人歇腳的小店；時候尚早，還沒有客人。屋旁一片平整的空地便是穀場，早春時節空空蕩蕩，只立著一副木架和一根叉竿；一株截了頂的老柳，新枝像扇子般張開。故宮名畫記稱這一景為「寂靜的穀場」，余輝的小題作「曬場農舍」。
S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・畫中所見
S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225.long_en: Past the little bridge, a few farmhouses line the road, with awnings and chairs and benches in front, like a small inn for travellers to rest; it is early and there are no customers yet. The flat open ground beside them is the threshing floor, empty in early spring, with only a wooden frame and a forked pole standing on it; an old willow with its crown cut off spreads new shoots like a fan. The Palace Museum's notes call this scene “the silent threshing floor,” and Yu Hui's subtitle for it is “Drying Yard and Farmhouses.”
S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · What the painting shows

S1.grd.bank_31660.long: 汴河開鑿於隋煬帝時，沿河的堤岸便叫隋堤，堤上遍植楊柳，「隋堤煙柳」後來列為「汴京八景」之一。畫中的柳樹樹幹蒼老扭曲，枝頭卻是新抽的嫩條。故宮名畫記解釋：堤柳長到一定粗細，就砍去樹梢，砍下的枝條紮成捆，釘在兩岸防洪護堤，年年如此，才長成這副頭大身粗的模樣。
S1.grd.bank_31660.cite: 故宮名畫記・畫中所見
S1.grd.bank_31660.long_en: The Bian Canal was dug in the time of Emperor Yang of Sui, so the embankment along it is called the Sui Embankment, and willows were planted all along it; “Misty Willows on the Sui Embankment” later became one of the “Eight Sights of Bianjing.” The painted willows have old, twisted trunks, but their branches carry fresh new shoots. The Palace Museum's notes explain that when embankment willows reach a certain thickness their tops are cut off, and the cut branches are tied in bundles and pinned along both banks against floods; done year after year, it gives the trees this big-headed, thick-trunked shape.
S1.grd.bank_31660.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · What the painting shows

S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.long: 一隊人馬從郊外掃墓回城：轎頂插滿楊柳，柳條一直垂到轎身，轎夫一前一後抬著；挑夫擔著箱籠，騎馬的男主人隨在隊後。轎子關著，看不見裏面的人，故宮名畫記說坐的是女主人。這正是《東京夢華錄》寫的清明風俗：城裏人出郊拜掃，回城時把楊柳雜花裝簇在轎頂上。畫面從這裏由靜轉動，人馬漸漸多了起來。
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.quote: 轎子即以楊柳雜花裝簇頂上，四垂遮映。
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.cite: 故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.long_en: A party is coming back to town from sweeping graves in the country: willow twigs are stuck all over the sedan's roof and hang down to its sides, carried by two bearers front and back, while a porter carries trunks on a pole and the male head of the household rides at the rear. The sedan is closed, so we cannot see who is inside; the Palace Museum's notes say it is the lady of the house. This is exactly the Qingming custom described in Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital: city people go out to the suburbs to visit graves and, coming home, decorate the sedan roof with willow and mixed flowers. From here the picture turns from stillness to motion, and more and more people and horses appear.
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.quote_en: The sedan chair is decked on top with willow and mixed flowers, hanging down on all four sides to screen it.
S1.veh.sedan_willow_30805.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S5.bld.tax_office.long: 進了城門，街北緊貼城牆的頭一家，是一座敞開的廳屋，西間掛著一桿大秤，中間官員坐在長案後正要落筆。故宮名畫記說「有的研究者認為這是稅務所」：案上的紙卷或是「引子」，即商貨的通行憑證，沒有引子，稅就收得格外重。門外貨包堆著，貨主指著貨物和稅吏爭論，連城樓上的人也探頭張望。余輝更讀出一層意思：城門內頭一家本該是城防機關，如今卻改成了收稅的地方。
S5.bld.tax_office.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S5.bld.tax_office.long_en: Inside the gate, the first building on the north side of the street, hard against the city wall, is an open hall; a big steelyard hangs in the west bay, and in the middle an official sits behind a long desk about to put brush to paper. The Palace Museum's notes say “some researchers think this is a tax office”: the paper rolls on the desk may be the “yinzi,” a pass for merchants' goods, and without one the tax is charged especially heavy. Outside, bundles of goods are piled up, a merchant points at his goods and argues with the tax clerk, and even the people up on the gate tower lean out to look. Yu Hui reads one more layer into it: the first building inside a city gate ought to be a defence office, and here it has been turned into a place that collects tax.
S5.bld.tax_office.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S5.bld.wine_depot.long: 孫羊正店東邊一間臨街的屋子，地上排著打了鐵箍的大木桶，正是《東京夢華錄》說的「梢桶」，正店用它裝酒。桶上擱著水桶，一根滅火的麻搭橫在上面。余輝認出這本是防火的軍巡鋪屋，該存水的地方卻放滿了酒桶；屋裏的弓手有的拉弓試弦，有的綁護腕、繫護腰，準備押運禁軍的酒。故宮只說屋裏的人像在準備出發，韓森則以為這是賣弓箭的鋪子。這裏從余輝之說。
S5.bld.wine_depot.quote: 每坊巷三百步許，有軍巡鋪屋一所。
S5.bld.wine_depot.cite: 余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉・《東京夢華錄》・故宮名畫記・韓森
S5.bld.wine_depot.long_en: East of Sun Yang's Main Tavern is a street-front room where big wooden barrels with iron hoops stand in rows on the ground: the very “shaotong” casks that Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital describes, which main taverns use to carry wine. Buckets sit on top of the casks, and a fire-swab for putting out fires lies across them. Yu Hui recognises this as a patrol post for fire watch, where water should be stored but wine casks are piled instead; the archers inside are pulling bows to test the strings, or tying on wrist guards and waist guards, getting ready to escort the wine of the Imperial Guard. The Palace Museum says only that the people inside seem to be preparing to set out, and Hansen thinks it is a shop selling bows and arrows. Here we follow Yu Hui.
S5.bld.wine_depot.quote_en: Every three hundred paces along the wards and lanes there is one patrol post.
S5.bld.wine_depot.cite_en: Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Hansen

S5.str.gate_tower.long: 這是全卷最大的建築：廡殿頂，重重斗拱把屋簷挑得老遠，故宮說它有「大鵬展翅」的氣勢。樓內看得見一副鼓架，架著一面大鼓，余輝為這一景取名「城上暮鼓」。門額上只寫一個「門」字，城名用幾點帶過，余輝以為畫家有意不點明。樓門口獨立一人，余輝說是更夫，正低頭看稅務所前的爭吵；韓森卻說他是遊人，因為他望著城裏，不像守衛那樣望著城外。
S5.str.gate_tower.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・韓森
S5.str.gate_tower.long_en: This is the largest building in the whole scroll: a hip roof, with layer upon layer of brackets pushing the eaves far out, which the Palace Museum says has the bearing of a “great roc spreading its wings.” Inside, a drum stand with a great drum can be seen, and Yu Hui names this scene “Evening Drum on the City Wall.” The plaque bears only the single character “Gate,” and the name of the city is skipped over with a few dots; Yu Hui thinks the painter meant not to say. A lone figure stands at the tower door, whom Yu Hui calls the night watchman, looking down at the quarrel in front of the Tax Office; Hansen says he is a sightseer, because he looks toward the city rather than out toward the country as a guard would.
S5.str.gate_tower.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · Hansen

S5.str.moat_bridge.long: 護城河上一座平平的木橋，兩側有木欄，欄邊擠滿了看水的人，有的倚欄看春水游魚，有的背過身來閒談。兩個小乞兒伸著手向遊人討錢，故宮名畫記寫得仔細：有人裝作沒聽見，有人怕掃了雅興，給一文錢打發他們走。戴頭巾的讀書人和穿短衣的苦力在同一道橋欄邊並肩，韓森說這座橋是各色人等的一幅群像。
S5.str.moat_bridge.cite: 故宮名畫記・邵琦・韓森・畫中所見
S5.str.moat_bridge.long_en: A flat wooden bridge crosses the moat, with wooden rails on both sides, and the rails are crowded with people looking at the water; some lean over to watch the spring water and the fish, others turn their backs and chat. Two little beggar boys hold out their hands to passers-by, and the Palace Museum's notes describe it closely: some pretend not to hear, some, afraid of spoiling the pleasant mood, give a coin to send them off. A scholar in a headscarf and a labourer in a short jacket stand shoulder to shoulder at the same railing, and Hansen says this bridge is a group portrait of all kinds of people.
S5.str.moat_bridge.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Shao Qi · Hansen · What the painting shows

S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.long: 這是畫中最氣派的酒樓。臨街搭起高大的彩樓歡門，綴滿花枝；門前燈箱寫著「正店」「香醪」，另一隻只認得一個「孫」字。樓上窗裏坐滿了飲酒的客人。余輝說，「正店」是官府授權釀酒的酒店，其餘的小酒家叫「腳店」，多向正店打酒來賣。門口還立著葫蘆形的紅燈，故宮名畫記說叫「梔子燈」，到了宋代成了酒店有妓女陪酒的標記。
S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.quote: 在京正店七十二戶，此外不能遍數，其餘皆謂之腳店。
S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.long_en: This is the most imposing tavern in the painting. A tall festive welcome gate of silk and flowers is raised along the street, hung all over with blossoms; the lantern boxes in front read “Main Tavern” and “Fragrant Wine,” and another shows only the character “Sun.” Guests fill the windows upstairs, drinking. Yu Hui explains that a “main tavern” was a wine house officially licensed to brew, while the smaller wine houses were called “leg taverns” and mostly bought their wine from main taverns to resell. At the door also stand red gourd-shaped lanterns, which the Palace Museum's notes call “gardenia lanterns”; by the Song they had become a sign that a tavern had women to keep drinkers company.
S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.quote_en: In the capital there are seventy-two main taverns, besides others too many to count; the rest are all called leg taverns.
S6.bld.sunyang_zhengdian.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.long: 街角的肉鋪掛著一面白布長幌，寫著「孫羊店」。余輝讀作孫記正店開的羊肉分號：簷下掛著羊肺、羊腸、羊肝、羊肚，價牌上寫著「□斤六十足」。這個「足」字，是說店家要足數的錢，不收打了折扣的「省陌」。也有人把案上掛的讀作一扇豬肉。故宮名畫記又說，門口板凳上坐著個胖老闆，讓人想起《水滸傳》裏的「鎮關西」鄭屠。
S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.quote: 都市錢陌，官用七十七，街市通用七十五，魚肉菜七十二陌。
S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》
S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.long_en: The butcher's shop on the corner hangs a long white cloth banner reading “Sun Yang Shop.” Yu Hui reads it as a lamb branch of Sun's main tavern: under the eaves hang lamb lungs, intestines, liver and tripe, and the price tag reads “[?] jin, sixty full.” That word “full” means the shopkeeper wants a full count of coins and will not take the discounted “short string.” Some read what hangs on the counter as a side of pork. The Palace Museum's notes add that the fat shopkeeper sitting on a bench at the door recalls Butcher Zheng, “Zhenguanxi,” in Water Margin.
S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.quote_en: The city's strings of cash: official use seventy-seven to the string, general use in the streets seventy-five, fish, meat and vegetables seventy-two.
S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital

S6.fig.storyteller_3822.long: 肉鋪門前，一圈人圍著一位大鬍子說書人。他面朝外，聽眾大多背對著我們，聽得入神。余輝說這是全卷唯一一處公開的表演，圍聽的有僧人、道士、讀書人，也有婦人孩子。故宮名畫記說，城市興起了廣大的市民，北宋的娛樂業跟著興盛，雜劇、唱曲、傀儡戲、講史、小說樣樣都有，還出了不少名角。
S6.fig.storyteller_3822.quote: 霍四究，說《三分》。尹常賣，《五代史》。
S6.fig.storyteller_3822.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S6.fig.storyteller_3822.long_en: In front of the butcher's, a circle of people gathers around a bearded storyteller. He faces outward while most of the listeners have their backs to us, absorbed. Yu Hui says this is the only public performance in the whole scroll; the crowd includes monks, Daoists, scholars, and women and children. The Palace Museum's notes say that as a mass of townspeople arose, entertainment flourished in Northern Song, with variety plays, singing, puppet shows, history telling and storytelling all on offer, and many famous performers emerged.
S6.fig.storyteller_3822.quote_en: Huo Sijiu tells the Three Kingdoms. Yin Changmai tells the History of the Five Dynasties.
S6.fig.storyteller_3822.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S6.bld.inn_wang_yuanwai.long: 街南一座兩層的客店，路邊招牌頂上兩個小字「久住」並排，下面寫著「王員外家」。故宮名畫記說，「久住」有老字號、靠得住的意思，是招徠客人的話。樓上窗裏，一位客人伏案讀書，牆上掛著字幅，桌上擺著文房用具，余輝稱這一景為「士子苦讀」。每逢科舉之年，京城住滿了進京赴考的士人；客店不但住人，也存放貨物，不少買賣就在店裏說合。
S6.bld.inn_wang_yuanwai.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・畫中所見
S6.bld.inn_wang_yuanwai.long_en: On the south side of the street stands a two-storey inn; on the roadside sign the two small characters “Long Stay” sit side by side at the top, and below is written “Wang the Squire's House.” The Palace Museum's notes say “Long Stay” suggests an old, dependable house, a phrase to draw guests. In an upstairs window a guest bends over a desk reading, with a scroll hung on the wall and writing tools on the table, a scene Yu Hui calls “The Scholar Studying Hard.” In examination years the capital filled with scholars arriving for the exams; an inn housed not only people but also goods, and many deals were struck right in the inn.
S6.bld.inn_wang_yuanwai.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · What the painting shows

S6.bld.incense_shop_liu.long: 十字路口斜對角是一家香鋪，門前招牌寫著「劉家上色沉檀揀香」：上等的沉香、檀香，都是揀選過的好貨。招牌最末一字被行人的帽子擋住，學者讀作「香」。故宮名畫記說，香料在宋朝的進口貨裏佔了不小的份量，海外貿易甚至被稱為「香料貿易」；香料成了茶、鹽、礬之外，替官府賺取巨利的大宗貨物，買賣也受官府管制。
S6.bld.incense_shop_liu.cite: 故宮名畫記・畫中所見
S6.bld.incense_shop_liu.long_en: On the diagonal corner of the crossroads is an incense shop, with a sign at the door reading “Liu Family, Finest Selected Aloeswood and Sandalwood”: top-grade aloeswood and sandalwood, hand-picked goods. The last character on the sign is blocked by a passer-by's hat, and scholars read it as “incense.” The Palace Museum's notes say spices made up no small share of Song imports, so that overseas trade was even called the “spice trade”; spices, alongside tea, salt and alum, became a major source of great profit for the government, and trade in them was controlled by the state.
S6.bld.incense_shop_liu.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · What the painting shows

S6.fig.jie_old_man_2138.long: 十字街西南角，一塊招牌斜倚簷下，上面掛著一個「解」字，竹棚裏一群穿儒生衣冠的年輕人，圍著一位老者或坐或立。這個「解」字怎麼讀，說法不一：故宮以為科舉與「解」字關係密切，這是替舉子辦理應考手續的地方，年輕人是來打聽考試消息的；余輝讀作算命鋪，舉子們在考前求問前程，並把這裏列為結尾「三問」中的問命；香港的教材則說它是當鋪。這裏取故宮之說。
S6.fig.jie_old_man_2138.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S6.fig.jie_old_man_2138.long_en: At the south-west corner of the crossroads a sign leans under the eaves bearing the single character “Jie,” and inside a bamboo shed a group of young men in scholars' dress sit or stand around an old man. How to read “Jie” is disputed: the Palace Museum holds that the character is closely tied to the civil-service examinations, that this is a place that handles applications for candidates, and that the young men are asking for exam news; Yu Hui reads it as a fortune-teller's shop, where candidates ask about their prospects before the exam, and lists it as the question about fate among the closing “three questions”; a Hong Kong textbook says it is a pawnshop. Here we take the Palace Museum's reading.
S6.fig.jie_old_man_2138.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S6.str.square_well_2000.long: 十字街西頭的水井邊，幾個人正在打水：一個站在井架上拉著井繩，一個彎腰把水桶提上來，一個把滿桶扛上肩頭。井口用木樑架成「田」字，故宮名畫記說這樣可以幾個人同時打水，又說這口井並不深；余輝則說這是富人街坊的官井，井口架上橫樑，是怕人失足落井。這麼大的京城，吃水用水本是一件大事。
S6.str.square_well_2000.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・畫中所見
S6.str.square_well_2000.long_en: At the well at the west end of the crossroads, several people are drawing water: one stands on the well frame hauling the rope, one bends to lift up the bucket, and one swings a full bucket onto his shoulder. The well-mouth is framed with timber beams in the shape of the character “field,” which the Palace Museum's notes say lets several people draw water at once, adding that the well is not deep; Yu Hui says instead that this is the official well of a wealthy neighbourhood, and that crossbeams were put over the mouth so no one would fall in. In so large a capital, getting water was a matter of real importance.
S6.str.square_well_2000.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · What the painting shows

S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.long: 路北一座寺院，山門緊閉，門扇上一排排門釘，兩側木欄後坐著天王塑像。一位穿袈裟的僧人正從旁邊的小門走進寺裏。故宮名畫記說，山門簷下有斗拱，似乎還掛著匾額，可見這座寺院等級不低；余輝則留意到，匾上的寺名只用幾點帶過，和城門一樣，畫家有意不寫明是哪一處。汴京有名的寺院，有大相國寺、開寶寺、太平興國寺。
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.quote: 每日交五更，諸寺院行者打鐵牌子或木魚循門報曉。
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.quoteSrc: 《東京夢華錄》卷三〈天曉諸人入市〉
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.long_en: On the north side of the road stands a temple, its main gate shut, the doors studded with rows of nails and guardian-king statues seated behind wooden railings on either side. A monk in a kasaya is walking through a small side door into the temple. The Palace Museum's notes say the gate has brackets under its eaves and seems to have carried a plaque, a sign of a temple of no low rank; Yu Hui adds that the temple's name on the plaque is skipped over with a few dots, just like the city gate, the painter deliberately not saying which one. Bianjing's famous temples include Daxiangguo Temple, Kaibao Temple and Taiping Xingguo Temple.
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.quote_en: Every day at the fifth watch, the temples' attendants strike iron plates or wooden fish and go from door to door announcing the dawn.
S4.bld.temple_gate_hall_9960.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows

S4.bld.post_gatehouse_11730.long: 一座院落，紅漆大門釘著門釘，門扇上貼著告示，土牆上插著竹簽。門外一群兵卒或坐或臥，有的抱膝打盹，有的趴在文書箱上睡著了，槍矛、旗子靠在牆邊；院裏一匹白馬也躺著。故宮以為這是傳遞公文的遞鋪，設在城門外，城門夜裏關了，官差也有處歇宿。余輝讀作「懶兵候主」：一早就該動身，差官卻遲遲不出來。韓森則說它像兵營、衙門，甚至是監獄。
S4.bld.post_gatehouse_11730.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉・韓森・畫中所見
S4.bld.post_gatehouse_11730.long_en: A courtyard with a red-lacquered gate studded with nails, a notice pasted on the door, and bamboo slips stuck into the earthen wall. Outside, a group of soldiers sit or lie around, some hugging their knees dozing, some asleep on document boxes, with spears and flags leaning against the wall; in the yard a white horse is lying down too. The Palace Museum takes it for a dispatch post for passing official papers, placed outside the city gate so that when the gate is shut at night officials on errands still have somewhere to sleep. Yu Hui reads it as “lazy soldiers awaiting their master”: they should have set off at dawn, but the officer is slow to appear. Hansen says it looks like a barracks, a government office, even a prison.
S4.bld.post_gatehouse_11730.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · Hansen · What the painting shows

S4.fig.fortune_teller_12232.long: 路邊一座蓆棚下，算命先生戴著黑帽坐在長桌後，一位白衣客人坐在桌頭，探身聽他推算；棚下掛著招牌「看命」「神課」，還有一塊學者讀作「決疑」。故宮名畫記說，宋人篤信陰陽五行、推步占卜，照王安石的說法，京城以此為生的人極多；有術士誇口「士大夫的命運，在我可否之間」，難怪這位先生把攤子支在官衙旁邊。
S4.fig.fortune_teller_12232.cite: 故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S4.fig.fortune_teller_12232.long_en: By the roadside, under a mat awning, a fortune-teller in a black hat sits behind a long table, and a customer in white sits at the head of it, leaning in to hear his calculations; signs hung under the awning read “Reading Fates” and “Divination,” and another that scholars read as “Settling Doubts.” The Palace Museum's notes say the Song people firmly believed in yin-yang and the five phases, in calculation and divination, and that by Wang Anshi's account a great many people in the capital lived by it; one diviner even boasted that “the fate of the scholar-officials lies in my yes or no,” so no wonder this man set up his stall right beside a government office.
S4.fig.fortune_teller_12232.quote_en: Those who sell medicine or tell fortunes all wear proper caps and sashes.
S4.fig.fortune_teller_12232.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.long: 路口一停一走兩輛大車，車頂鋪著厚厚的棕毛，像一座蓬鬆的草屋。這是給家眷坐的車子，《東京夢華錄》叫它「宅眷坐車子」。故宮名畫記看見走著的那輛車後門裏，一位婦人低頭撩起簾子往外望；車前一牛駕轅、一牛拉套，後面跟著提食物的僕從，騎馬戴帽的大概就是男主人，一行人也許剛從郊外掃墓回來。
S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.quote: 又有宅眷坐車子，與平頭車大抵相似，但棕作蓋。
S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.cite: 故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.long_en: At the junction, two big carts, one halted and one moving, have thick palm fibre spread over their roofs like fluffy thatched huts. These are carts for a family's women, called “carts for household ladies” in Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital. The Palace Museum's notes see, in the rear door of the cart that is moving, a lady lowering her head to lift the curtain and look out; an ox is in the shafts and another is hitched on, servants follow behind carrying food, and the capped rider is probably the master of the house, the party perhaps just back from sweeping graves in the country.
S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.quote_en: There are also carts for household ladies, much like flat-topped carts, but with a palm-fibre cover.
S4b.veh.palm_cart_13070.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.long: 小飯鋪北邊是一家修大車的鋪子，棚下堆著方木、長桿，大概是做車轅、車軸的料。一個匠人彎著腰，伏在一隻平放在地上的大車輪上幹活；故宮名畫記說他雙手握著榔頭，正在修整車輪。城門口外，牛車、棕蓋車往來不絕。余輝為這一景取名「車鋪勞作」。
S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.quote: 東京般載車，大者曰『太平』。
S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・畫中所見
S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.long_en: North of the small eating shop is a shop that repairs big carts, with squared timbers and long poles piled under its awning, probably material for making shafts and axles. A craftsman bends over a big cart wheel laid flat on the ground at his work; the Palace Museum's notes say he grips a mallet in both hands and is trimming the wheel. Outside the city gate, ox carts and palm-roofed carts come and go without end. Yu Hui names this scene “Work at the Cartwright's.”
S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.quote_en: The goods-carrying carts of the Eastern Capital: the largest is called the “Taiping.”
S4b.bld.wheelwright_shed_13840.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · What the painting shows

S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.long: 路北一座敞開的廳堂，前頭搭著蓆棚，棚下擺著長桌條凳。一位戴寬簷黑帽的客人探身向前，和對面一個翹著腿的白衣胖漢說話；另一位戴黑帽的，兩肘支在桌上歇著。屋上不見招牌，是不是茶鋪，還說不準；余輝為這一景取名「小鋪閒坐」。城門口外這一段，處處是這樣不慌不忙的人。
S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.quote: 更有提茶瓶之人，每日鄰里互相支茶，相問動靜。
S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.cite: 余輝・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.long_en: On the north side of the road is an open hall with a mat awning in front, long tables and benches set out beneath it. A guest in a wide-brimmed black hat leans forward to talk to a stout man in white sitting opposite with his legs crossed; another man in a black hat rests with both elbows on the table. There is no sign on the roof, so whether it is a teahouse is not certain; Yu Hui names this scene “Sitting at the Little Shop.” This stretch outside the city gate is full of unhurried people like these.
S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.quote_en: There are also those who carry teapots, and every day neighbours set out tea for each other and ask after one another's news.
S4b.bld.tea_house_14531.cite_en: Yu Hui · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

S3.str.rainbow_bridge.long: 這座橋沒有一根橋柱，用大木一根根交錯穿插，架成一道拱，橫跨汴河。汴河水勢暴漲暴落，有柱的橋年年被沖壞；無柱的木拱不受激流衝擊，經久不壞。據《澠水燕談錄》，這種「飛橋」最早是青州一名牢城廢卒想出來的，後來汴河上都照樣建造，俗稱虹橋。明清的仿本把它畫成了石拱橋，故宮說這段原畫對研究宋代橋樑異常珍貴。
S3.str.rainbow_bridge.quote: 其橋無柱，皆以巨木虛架，飾以丹雘，宛如飛虹。
S3.str.rainbow_bridge.cite: 《東京夢華錄》・《澠水燕談錄》・故宮名畫記
S3.str.rainbow_bridge.long_en: This bridge has not a single pier. Great timbers are interwoven one over another to make an arch across the Bian Canal. The Bian's waters rise and fall violently, and bridges with piers were wrecked year after year; a pier-less timber arch is not struck by the rushing current and lasts. According to Mianshui Yantan Lu, this kind of “flying bridge” was first thought up by a discharged soldier of a prison camp in Qingzhou, and afterwards the same was built all along the Bian, commonly called the Rainbow Bridge. Copies from the Ming and Qing paint it as a stone arch, and the Palace Museum says this stretch of the original painting is extraordinarily precious for studying Song bridges.
S3.str.rainbow_bridge.quote_en: The bridge has no piers; it is spanned in the air with huge timbers, decked in cinnabar red, like a flying rainbow.
S3.str.rainbow_bridge.cite_en: Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Mianshui Yantan Lu · Palace Museum, Minghuaji

S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.long: 橋頭的酒店，門前燈箱正面寫「腳店」，側面寫「十千」，合起來便是「十千腳店」。按《東京夢華錄》，京城正店之外的酒家都叫腳店，多向正店打酒來賣。這家腳店門樓頂上也搭起高聳的彩樓歡門，樓上坐著飲酒的客人，門外拴著一匹備了鞍的馬。門前一輛串車正在裝貨，故宮名畫記說貨物像一串串銅錢；余輝卻說車上蓋的是一面遭廢的草書屏風。
S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.quote: 其正酒店戶，見腳店三兩次打酒，便敢借與三五百兩銀器。
S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.cite: 《東京夢華錄》・故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉・畫中所見
S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.long_en: The tavern at the bridgehead has a lantern box in front reading “Leg Tavern” on its face and “Shiqian” on its side, which together make “Shiqian Leg Tavern.” According to Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital, wine houses in the capital other than the main taverns are all called leg taverns, and mostly buy their wine from main taverns to resell. This leg tavern also has a tall festive welcome gate raised over its gatehouse, guests drinking upstairs, and a saddled horse tied outside. In front a string cart is being loaded; the Palace Museum's notes say the goods look like strings of copper coins, while Yu Hui says what is covered on the cart is a discarded cursive-script screen.
S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.quote_en: When a main tavern has seen a leg tavern come for wine two or three times, it will dare lend it three or five hundred taels of silver vessels.
S3.bld.tavern_gate_16870.cite_en: Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · What the painting shows

S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.long: 腳店前立著一根高桿，桿頂有隻鳥形的風標，橫桿上垂下一面長旗，寫著「新酒」。故宮名畫記說，宋代酒稅收入極高，官府對酒實行專賣；「新酒」特指中秋前後開賣的酒，開賣時還要舉行隆重的迎酒儀式。也正因如此，孔憲易拿這面旗作證，說畫的是秋天。汴河岸邊另有一面「小酒」旗，可見當時飲酒風氣之盛。
S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.quote: 中秋節前，諸店皆賣新酒，重新結絡門面彩樓花頭。
S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.cite: 故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・孔憲易
S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.long_en: In front of the leg tavern stands a tall pole topped with a bird-shaped weathervane, and from a crosspiece hangs a long flag reading “New Wine.” The Palace Museum's notes say that wine taxes in the Song were very high and the government held a monopoly on wine; “new wine” means wine that goes on sale around the Mid-Autumn Festival, opened with a grand ceremony of welcoming the wine. For this reason Kong Xianyi cites this flag as evidence that the painting shows autumn. Another flag, “Small Wine,” stands on the bank of the Bian, a sign of how strong the habit of drinking was then.
S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.quote_en: Before the Mid-Autumn Festival, all the taverns sell new wine and put up fresh flower-topped festive gates on their fronts.
S3.prop.xinjiu_flagpole_17630.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Kong Xianyi

colophons.title: 卷後題跋
colophons.lead: 畫卷之後，接裱著金、元、明歷代文人的題跋。張擇端的生平，就靠這些題跋才留了下來；後人怎樣讀這幅畫，也寫在這裏。

items.text: 翰林張擇端，字正道，東武人也。幼讀書，遊學於京師，後習繪事。本工其界畫，尤嗜於舟車、市橋郭徑，別成家數也。
items.gloss: 畫家的生平，只有這一段。張著又據《向氏評論圖畫記》說此圖選入「神品」，落款「大定丙午清明後一日」，余輝以為這是婉轉點明了畫中時節。

items.text: 通衢車馬正喧闐，祗是宣和第幾年。當日翰林呈畫本，升平風物正堪傳。
items.gloss: 後人據這首詩把畫定在宣和年間，又從「升平風物」讀出太平盛世；他的另一句「水門東去接隋渠」，則讓人把城門讀作東水門。

items.text: 楚柂吳檣萬里舡，橋南橋北好風煙。喚回一餉繁華夢，簫鼓樓臺若個邊。
items.gloss: 看過畫的金人，大多是在汴京淪陷之後懷想故都。

items.text: 畫橋虹臥浚儀渠，兩岸風煙天下無。滿眼而今皆瓦礫，人猶時復得璣珠。
items.gloss: 他說如今滿眼都是瓦礫，人們還不時從中拾到珠玉。
李祁從畫裏讀出的不只是繁華，還有憂慮與警惕，余輝說他是第一個看出此畫門道的人。
李祁的後人李東陽，看畫時想到的是興衰。
邵寶以為畫家在盛世之中寄寓憂危。這段跋文在明末被裁去，後人在《式古堂書畫彙考》裏找回了它。
